_purpose: Every number the paper cites lives here once, with the run and artifact it is re-derived from. tools/constants/check.py and audit.py enforce it; tools/constants/export.py writes the paper's macros from it.

_schema.value: the number (or list, or an object where a reader indexes one number per key); null means not yet measured, and the note says why
_schema.card: the GPU the number is about, as the machine reported it; 'none' for a number about no card
_schema.context: the context length C the number was measured at; 'n/a' where it does not apply
_schema.timing_scope: one of _timing_scopes, or 'n/a' for a number that is not a time or a rate
_schema.run: required on measured: the runs/<run-id> directory whose artifact the audit re-derives the value from
_schema.artifact: required on measured: the file in that run directory
_schema.inputs: projected only: the constants keys the cost model read
_schema.note: one or two sentences; for external, the URL

_grades.measured: made by a driver in this repository; audit.py re-derives it from `artifact` in `run`
_grades.derived: arithmetic over other entries; check.py recomputes it from the entries it names
_grades.projected: the cost model or another projection, with its inputs named; never presented as a measurement
_grades.external: read from a public source, with its URL in the note
_grades.asserted: an assumption the owner made, with the reason in the note

_timing_scopes.commit: the commitment path only: interpolation, low-degree extension and Merkle hashing of the committed trees
_timing_scopes.stwo total: commit plus the prover's own call: constraint evaluation, quotients, out-of-domain sampling, FRI
_timing_scopes.whole wall: trace generation, interaction generation, stwo total and serialization, summed per segment; it does not include reading the witness or building the layer
_timing_scopes.loop: the one-process segment loop's own wall-clock time, which does include the witness read and the layer build; pipelined loops overlap one segment's generation with another's proving
_timing_scopes.primitive: one primitive of the proof system on its own (a hash, a field operation, a lookup, a fold), timed by the vendored library's benchmark harness; not a scope of any proof and not comparable with the four above
_timing_scopes.verify: the verifier's side, on the host's own cores and not on the card: one segment's call over its serialized statement, claims and proof, or the grid pass that checks the links between segments. It is not a scope of the prover and is not comparable with the four above.
_timing_scopes.unproved prefill: one `max_new_tokens=1` call on the unproved model with the weights already resident: the whole prompt read and the first generated position emitted. Nothing is proved in it.
_timing_scopes.unproved decode: the rest of the same full call, by difference: the remaining generated positions, one step each, with the weights already resident. Nothing is proved in it.
_timing_scopes.unproved end to end: the full call on its own: the prompt prefilled and every generated position decoded, as one wall-clock time, with the weights already resident. Nothing is proved in it.
_timing_scopes.extraction: the witness extraction: the forward passes that write the dumps the proofs read, on the card, timed by the driver around each pass. It is outside the prover, so it is in none of the four proving scopes; it does not include emitting the device kernels, installing them or rebuilding.
_timing_scopes.cold whole wall: the extraction the proofs read plus whole wall: what the sequence costs on a host that holds no witness dump yet. Kernel emission, the install and the rebuild are not in it.
_timing_scopes.cold loop: the extraction the proofs read plus loop: what the sequence costs on a host that holds no witness dump yet. Kernel emission, the install and the rebuild are not in it.
_timing_scopes.trace generation: generating one segment's base trace, the prover's own `trace_secs`. It is inside whole wall and is not one of the four whole-proof scopes; on the device backend it overlaps interaction generation, so the two are not a split of anything.
_timing_scopes.interaction generation: generating one segment's LogUp interaction columns and running the GKR reductions over them, the prover's own `interaction_secs`. Inside whole wall, like trace generation, and overlapping it on the device backend.
_timing_scopes.loop phase: one of the twelve terms the segment loop partitions into when one segment is in flight: the witness read, its decode, check, construct and alloc and what they leave of the build; base-trace generation; interaction generation; stwo total; serialization; what those leave of the proving half; and what the segments leave of the loop. Each is measured, none is inside another, and the twelve add to the loop scope exactly. A pipelined loop has no such split: two segments' phases overlap in time and the same fields add to more than the loop.

cost.h100_reference_usd_per_hour.note: RunPod published on-demand list price, Secure Cloud tier, H100 SXM 80 GB, https://www.runpod.io/gpu-models/h100-sxm (page updated 2026-08-27, retrieved 2026-08-31). Paired with the H200 rate from the same provider, tier and date.

cost.h200_reference_usd_per_hour.note: RunPod published on-demand list price, Secure Cloud tier, H200 141 GB, https://www.runpod.io/gpu-models/h200 (page updated 2026-08-27, retrieved 2026-08-31). The higher tier is the conservative choice for a cost claim.

hardware.h200.hbm_gbps_spec.note: NVIDIA H200 data sheet, HBM3e memory bandwidth, https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/h200/. A specification figure; this project never measured the card's own bandwidth.

deepprove.tpm_seq512_basefold.note: DeepProve, https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/1112, Table 2, sequence length 512 with the BaseFold commitment: 512 tokens / 2.94 min. Their time counts proving only and excludes quantized inference and trace recording, which our whole-wall and loop scopes include; their attention depth is bounded by the sequence length.

verinf.maverick.positions.note: VerInf, https://github.com/JamesPetrie/VerInf, section 9: one forward pass over a 500-token prompt and a 500-token greedy continuation, all 1000 positions proved.

verinf.maverick.prover_hours.note: VerInf, https://github.com/JamesPetrie/VerInf, section 9: Llama-4-Maverick (400B parameters, 17B active), the 1000-position forward pass, prover peak 78.1 GB of GPU memory.

verinf.maverick.tok_s.note: verinf.maverick.positions / (verinf.maverick.prover_hours x 3600). Not a number they state; all 1000 positions are proved where our decode rows prove output tokens only.

verinf.maverick.proof_gb.note: VerInf, https://github.com/JamesPetrie/VerInf, section 9: 40 opened columns; proof size grows linearly with the witness at their fixed parameters.

verinf.maverick.verify_hours.note: VerInf, https://github.com/JamesPetrie/VerInf, section 9: verification on 20 CPU cores, peak 75.7 GB; interactive, per-challenge soundness about 2^-16.6.

verinf.maverick.bound_bits_per_token.note: VerInf, https://github.com/JamesPetrie/VerInf, section 9: the bound on unexplained information per token over the 500-token continuation. Their statement bounds information; it does not prove the exact computation or the token choice.

verinf.llama2_7b.prover_minutes.note: VerInf, https://github.com/JamesPetrie/VerInf, section 9: Llama-2-7B, 32 layers, real checkpoint weights, prover peak 11.2 GB, 1.44 GB proof at 10 opened columns.

verinf.gb10_measured_bandwidth_gbps.note: VerInf, https://github.com/JamesPetrie/VerInf, appendix A.5: the memory bandwidth their NTT is bound by, as they measured it, not the GB10's specification figure.

verinf.gb10_vs_h200_bandwidth_ratio.note: verinf.gb10_measured_bandwidth_gbps / hardware.h200.hbm_gbps_spec: their measured rate over an NVIDIA specification figure. Our commitment path is bound by hashing, not by memory bandwidth, so this compares hardware classes and nothing else.

cells.headline.c4096.fresh.note: Fresh committed cells over the sequence's 290 segments, added up from the run's 5 slice outputs; 78.967 M per proved position.

secs.headline.c4096.commit.note: The commitment path, added up over every segment of the sequence.

secs.headline.c4096.stwo_total.note: Commit plus the prover's own call, added up over every segment.

secs.headline.c4096.whole_wall.note: Trace generation, interaction generation, stwo total and serialization, added up per segment; it does not count reading the witness or building the segment, which is what the loop scope adds.

secs.headline.c4096.loop.note: The 5 segment-loop processes' own wall-clock time added up. It counts reading the witness and building the segment, and each segment's generation overlaps the previous one's proving, so it is neither a subset nor a superset of the whole-wall row.

segments.headline.c4096.note: 9 token blocks of 32 layer segments, and an output head segment over the last prompt block and over the generated block. Two heads and not one, because a generated position's id has to equal the argmax proved for the position before it and the position before the first generated one is the last of the prompt (docs/decisions).

positions.headline.c4096.note: 4096 prompt positions and 512 output positions, every one of them proved from the embedding up through all 32 layers.

mem.headline.c4096.peak_mib.note: The most the card reported holding at any moment of the segment loop, sampled once a second. The card has 81,559 MiB.

pos_s.headline.c4096.whole_wall.note: positions.headline.c4096 / secs.headline.c4096.whole_wall. Positions and not tokens: the prompt is proved as well as the output (docs/decisions).

pos_s.headline.c4096.loop.note: positions.headline.c4096 / secs.headline.c4096.loop. Positions and not tokens: the prompt is proved as well as the output (docs/decisions).

secs_per_position.headline.c4096.whole_w.note: secs.headline.c4096.whole_wall / positions.headline.c4096. What one proved position cost, which is what the paper quotes instead of an overhead multiple (docs/decisions).

secs_per_position.headline.c4096.loop.note: secs.headline.c4096.loop / positions.headline.c4096. What one proved position cost, which is what the paper quotes instead of an overhead multiple (docs/decisions).

usd_per_1k_positions.headline.c4096.whol.note: secs.headline.c4096.whole_wall / positions.headline.c4096, at cost.h100_reference_usd_per_hour. The rate is a published list price and names its source; the card was rented at another price and that price is not a number about this measurement.

usd_per_1k_positions.headline.c4096.loop.note: secs.headline.c4096.loop / positions.headline.c4096, at cost.h100_reference_usd_per_hour. The rate is a published list price and names its source; the card was rented at another price and that price is not a number about this measurement.

secs_per_segment.headline.c4096.whole_wa.note: secs.headline.c4096.whole_wall / segments.headline.c4096. What one of the sequence's 290 segments cost on average. A segment's own cost grows with the prefix its token block reads, so this is the plan's mean and not any one segment's time.

secs_per_segment.headline.c4096.loop.note: secs.headline.c4096.loop / segments.headline.c4096. The same average at the scope that counts reading the witness and building the segment.

secs_per_layer.headline.c4096.loop.note: secs.headline.c4096.loop / 32, the model's layers. What proving every position of the sequence at one layer cost, so a claim that samples k of the 32 layers prices its sampled part at k times this. The two output head segments sit in the loop seconds and are not a layer, which puts about 0.7 per cent of this row on the head and not on a layer.

secs_per_layer_segment.headline.c4096.wh.note: secs.headline.c4096.whole_wall / the same 288 layer segments. The whole-wall scope does not count reading the witness or building the segment, which is what the loop row beside it adds. A head segment sits at the layer coordinate past the last layer, proves no attention and commits no boundary tree for the keys and values, so it is not a layer segment; both recorded plans carry two of them, one over the last prompt block and one over the generated block.

secs_per_layer_segment.headline.c4096.lo.note: secs.headline.c4096.loop / the sequence's 288 layer segments, which is segments.headline.c4096 less its two output head segments. What one layer segment cost on average at the scope that counts reading the witness and building the segment, so a claim that checks a fraction of the layers is priced on this row and a claim that checks a fraction of the proofs is priced on secs_per_segment.headline.c4096.loop, which counts the heads as well. A head segment sits at the layer coordinate past the last layer, proves no attention and commits no boundary tree for the keys and values, so it is not a layer segment; both recorded plans carry two of them, one over the last prompt block and one over the generated block.

share.headline.c4096.commit_of_stwo_tota.note: secs.headline.c4096.commit / secs.headline.c4096.stwo_total: the commitment path's share of the proof system's own call, over the whole sequence. The commitment path is inside that call, so this is a share and lies between 0 and 1.

share.headline.c4096.stwo_total_of_whole.note: secs.headline.c4096.stwo_total / secs.headline.c4096.whole_wall: the proof system's own share of the per-segment wall-clock time summed over the sequence, 5.20 per cent. The rest is trace generation, interaction generation and serialization, which the whole-wall scope also counts.

share.headline.c4096.commit_of_loop.note: secs.headline.c4096.commit / secs.headline.c4096.loop: the commitment path's share of the segment loop, 4.64 per cent. The loop is the scope that also reads the witness and builds the segment, which is why this is below the share of the proof system's own call above it. The gkr-ablation-c4096 entry says the commitment path is 5 per cent of the loop; that is that run's own 32-segment sample of one token block and not this sequence.

proof.headline.c4096.total_bytes.note: The serialized proofs of the sequence's 290 segments as the prover wrote them, added up: 18.46 GiB, one segment 48.4 to 120.0 MiB. This run kept every proof whole to the end, so grid.json holds all 290 true sizes and the total is read off one artifact, where the run at context 16,384 has to assemble it from two. It is the proof the prover produced: nothing compresses or aggregates it.

proof.headline.c4096.total_in_memory_byt.note: The same 290 proofs as the prover held them before serialization, added up from the run's 5 slice outputs: 7.19 GiB, 38.9 per cent of the serialized total. A slice output reports both, `proof_bytes` for the proof structure's own size and `proof_ser_bytes` for the JSON the prover wrote; the paper's proof size is the serialized one, because that is what a verifier is given.

proof.headline.c4096.bytes_per_segment_m.note: The median segment's serialized proof, over the sequence's 290: 64.97 MiB, against 48.4 MiB for the smallest and 120.0 MiB for the largest. A median and not a mean, because a segment's proof grows with the prefix its token block reads; the sequence's own size is the total row, which is the sum.

proof.headline.c4096.total_bytes / segments.headline.c4096, which is 65.20 MiB: what one segment of this sequence cost in serialized bytes on average. The median row beside it is 0.35 per cent lower and is a segment the run actually proved. Both are kept because they answer different questions: a segment's proof grows with the prefix its token block reads, so the median is the segment a reader would meet and the mean is the per-segment figure that multiplies back to the sequence's total.

The mean serialized proof over the 32 layer segments of the last token block, the block whose prefix is the whole 4,096-token context: 78.1 MiB, against 65.20 MiB over all 290 segments of the sequence. It is the like-for-like point against a run that proves one token block at one prefix, which is what runs/2026-09-11-predict-13b-h100 does, and it exists so that comparison is a ratio of two recorded rows and not arithmetic done in prose. The output head segment over that block is not a layer segment and is not in it.

proof.headline.c4096.in_memory_bytes_per.note: The median segment's proof before serialization, over the sequence's 290: 25.33 MiB. The serialized median beside it is 2.56 times larger, which is the JSON encoding and not more proof.

proof.headline.c4096.total_in_memory_bytes / segments.headline.c4096, which is 25.39 MiB: one segment's proof before serialization on average, against 65.20 MiB after it. The median beside it is 0.22 per cent lower; the mean and the median are kept for the same reason as the serialized pair above.

proof.headline.c4096.total_in_memory_bytes / positions.headline.c4096, which is 1.60 MiB: the proof before serialization per proved position, 38.9 per cent of proof.headline.c4096.bytes_per_position. The serialized row is what the paper's proof size means, because that is what a verifier is given. Per position and not per token: the prompt is proved as well as the output (docs/decisions).

proof.headline.c4096.bytes_per_position.note: proof.headline.c4096.total_bytes / positions.headline.c4096, which is 4.10 MiB. Per position and not per token: the prompt is proved as well as the output (docs/decisions).

verify.headline.c4096.secs_total.note: The verifier's own seconds over the sequence's 290 segment proofs, added up. It ran on the run host's cores and not on the card. The final grid was given `--verify --prompt`, so every proof was replayed from its serialized statement, claims and proof in that one pass, which also checked the 537 links and every published id; the run recorded no wall-clock time of its own for that pass, so there is no link-check row at this context.

verify.headline.c4096.secs_per_segment_m.note: The median segment's verification, over the sequence's 290: 0.31 to 0.84 s. Reading the three documents adds 0.035 s to the median, which the grid records beside it as `wall_secs` and this row does not count.

verify.headline.c4096.secs_total / segments.headline.c4096: what checking one segment's proof cost on average, on the host's own cores. The median beside it is 0.97 per cent higher. Proving one took secs_per_segment.headline.c4096.loop, 12.70 s on the card, 30.9 times this row, and the two are not the same machine's seconds.

verify.headline.c4096.secs_per_position.note: verify.headline.c4096.secs_total / positions.headline.c4096: what checking one proved position cost, on the host's own cores, against secs_per_position.headline.c4096.loop of 0.799 s to prove it on the card, 30.9 times as much. It is the whole sequence's verification spread over the positions it proves and is no one position's own time: the verifier is called once per segment.

commitment.c4096.sha256.note: The published model commitment: the digest of one line per layer coordinate carrying the layer number, that layer's model root and the model hash the root was derived under, and nothing else. It moves when the commitment moves and not when the file is reformatted.

commitment.c4096.layers.note: 32 layers and the output head's coordinate after them. One model root each, and the derivation refuses to write a table whose rows disagree about a layer's root.

commitment.c4096.cells.note: The (layer, prefix width) cells the table was derived over, one per segment of headline-c4096's plan. Every one of them was compared against the published commitment.

controls.suite.designed_rejections.note: Controls the verifier refused for the reason each was written for, over the suite's five targets: one real layer segment of headline-c4096's plan, that segment again under the --probe filter, and the three synthetic shapes. A control passes only as a designed rejection, with accepts false and falsified naming the verdict fields the bend turned off; a crash is never a pass and a skip by name is counted apart.

controls.suite.accepted.note: Controls the verifier accepted, over the same five targets, counted from every target's own probe record. Any number but zero is a soundness failure, and the run's gate fails on it.

controls.suite.crashes.note: Targets whose process died rather than finishing its list. A crash is never a pass: the gate fails the run on one, and each target's exit code is recorded beside its output so a run that dies is visible as a crash and not as a missing file.

controls.real.c4096.designed_rejections.note: Controls refused as designed on the real segment: layer 16 of the last token block of headline-c4096's plan, proved from that plan's own line. The suite had never finished on a real segment before: at 32e8fae it died at the control after the one that moves three values off the master table, taking the 41 refusals before it (zk-prover #134).

controls.real.c4096.skipped_by_name.note: Controls the prover skipped on the real segment by name, with the reason in the record: the attention-output seam's and the model swap's. Both rebuild the segment around a second draw of the residual stream, which is the synthetic construction's, so on a dump the draw and not the binding under test is what a refusal would be about (zk-prover #24). A control skipped by name is not a control that passed, which is why it is counted apart from the rejections.

verify.headline.c16384.secs_total.note: The verifier's own seconds over the sequence's 1,058 segment proofs, added up. It ran on the run host's cores and not on the card, group by group as the run went and on whole proofs, before each group's proofs were shrunk, so the seconds come from eight artifacts as the size does: 1,024 segments from the seven verify-g<blocks>.json records and 34 from verify-fixup.json, which is why the artifact named here is the first of eight. REPRODUCE.md's 'Which check ran where' paragraph for this driver says why the final grid could not replay them.

verify.headline.c16384.secs_per_segment_.note: The median segment's verification, over the sequence's 1,058: 0.31 to 2.16 s. It is 1.83 times the median at context 4,096, where the median proof is 1.63 times smaller.

verify.headline.c16384.secs_total / segments.headline.c16384: what checking one segment's proof cost on average, on the host's own cores. The median beside it is 3.7 per cent lower, because the segments of the last token blocks read the longest prefix and are the expensive ones; at context 4,096 the two lie the other way round. Proving one took secs_per_segment.headline.c16384.loop, 20.40 s on the card, 25.9 times this row.

verify.headline.c16384.secs_per_position.note: verify.headline.c16384.secs_total / positions.headline.c16384: what checking one proved position cost, on the host's own cores, against secs_per_position.headline.c16384.loop of 1.278 s to prove it on the card, 25.9 times as much. It is the whole sequence's verification spread over the positions it proves and is no one position's own time: the verifier is called once per segment. The link check between the segments is verify.headline.c16384.link_check_secs and is not in it.

verify.headline.c16384.link_check_secs.note: The final grid over all 1,058 segments: every link between segments the plan implies, checked over the serialized statements and proofs, and every published id checked against the prompt or against the argmax a head proved for the position before it. It replayed no proof, because the proofs had been shrunk (REPRODUCE.md, 'Which check ran where'), so this is the link check on its own; the c4096 grid did both in one pass and recorded no time of its own.

verify.consumer.c16384.secs_per_segment_.note: One segment of the reference proof -- Llama-3.1-8B layer 16, S = 512, C = 16,384, the five reductions on -- replayed three times on four cores of an Intel Xeon Platinum 8468 under a 128 GiB memory cap and with no card: the median of the verifier's own seconds, over 42.91, 43.17 and 44.76. The process took 44.09 s of wall-clock time for it, the 161 MiB proof read off disk and parsed included. 42.25 s of the median is the one shape root the verifier derives from the published calibration and compares with the one the statement carries; the proof's own check is the 0.92 s left over, against 0.757 s for the median segment of the sequence on sixteen cores of the same machine.

verify.consumer.c16384.peak_rss_bytes.note: The median peak resident set size of the three replay processes, each read from its own /usr/bin/time report: 28.5 GiB to check one segment at this context, against a serialized proof of 161 MiB. It is the working set the verifier builds and not the proof, and it is what a machine has to hold: four cores and 32 GB of memory are enough for this segment. No smaller segment has been measured on a machine of this size.

verify.consumer.c16384.secs_total_sequen.note: verify.consumer.c16384.secs_per_segment_median times segments.headline.c16384: what the sequence's 1,058 segment proofs would cost to check on four cores, one segment at a time, at the median segment's seconds. mem.probe.c16384.pipelined_l0_peak_mib.note: Layer 0 and layer 1 together under the pipeline, which is the pair the headline loop forms at the start of every block and the only pair that holds the plan's largest segment. It peaked at what layer 0 peaked at alone, so the second segment in flight cost the card nothing even here.

mem.probe.c24576.decode_peak_mib.note: The most the card reported holding at any moment of one decode segment proved on its own with the pipeline off, sampled once a second: layer 16 of the last token block, whose prefix is the whole 24,576-token prompt and whose shape 12 of the block's 32 segments have. The card has 81,559 MiB, so it fits with 1,916 to spare. The prover's own high-water mark for the same segment is this number to the MiB. The comparable 16,384-token row is mem.probe.c16384.serial_peak_mib, 72,379 MiB, which is the largest of four segments of the same shape class proved in one process.

mem.probe.c24576.layer0_oom_peak_mib.note: Layer 0 of the same block, proved on its own, DID NOT FIT: the process exited 1 out of memory and this is the most the card reported holding before the allocation it could not serve, 486 MiB short of the card's 81,559. It is not a peak of a segment that was proved and there is no such number at this context: the segment needs more than the card has. Layer 0 carries the embedding gadget and is the largest segment of the plan, and it is the segment the headline loops' peaks are -- 78,843 MiB at context 16,384 against that loop's 78,799 -- so it is the segment mem.projected.* is a line through.

secs.probe.c24576.decode_loop.note: The one-process loop over the single layer-16 segment, the pipeline off. The same segment on the reference backend took 268.971 s in host memory and hashed to the same proof digest, dc56b8482e172eeb.

bits.probe.c24576.layer0_ao_acc.note: The attention output accumulator's width in layer 0 of the last token block, as the extraction measured it. It sums over the prefix, so it grows with the context: this is what the row below is a function of.

bits.probe.c24576.layer0_ao_no_wrap_marg.note: What is left of the attention output's no-wrap window in that segment: 1 + 16 + 8 + 6 = 31 of the field's 31, nothing spare. The window is an identity over the integers only while it holds, the two limbs must together cover the accumulator and the exponent window must cover jv - jo, so no wider decomposition recovers a bit. At context 32,768 the accumulator is 25 bits and the same window is 1 + 16 + 9 + 6 = 32, over by one: the extraction refuses layer 0 of the last block by name and the segment cannot be written, let alone proved. So 32,768 is not a memory question under this quantization variant, and the probe that would have asked it has no run directory: nothing was proved, so nothing carries a provenance block.

secs.probe.c16384.layer0_loop.note: Layer 0 of the last block, proved on its own with the pipeline off: one segment, and the slowest in the plan as well as the largest.

secs.probe.c16384.pipelined_l0_loop.note: Layers 0 and 1 under the pipeline: 75.31 s a segment against 94.67 s for layer 0 alone, so the pipeline helps on the pair that holds the largest segment too.

cells.microbench.compose_fresh.note: Fresh committed cells of the one synthetic segment this run proves, the prover's recorded sound shape with the five GKR reductions on. It is the denominator of the commitment rate below and nothing else; a segment this size is not a throughput row.

secs.microbench.compose_commit.note: The commitment path of that proof on the reference backend: interpolation, low-degree extension and Merkle hashing of the committed trees. Its low-degree test took 1.989 s of the same proof and its whole prove call 4.835 s.

model_constants.dequant_pow2_cells_per_a.note: Dequantization by a power-of-two scale, the marginal cells one accumulator adds with the shared tables left out; 1,048,576 accumulators, 16 per row. The tables are a fixed cost of the segment and are not multiplied by a count, which is why the marginal figure and not the with-tables one is the cost model's input.

model_constants.dequant_chain_cells_per_.note: Dequantization by the bf16 chain, on the same sweep and the same terms as the power-of-two row above. It costs 1.73 times as much per accumulator.

model_constants.attnout_int8_cells_per_a.note: The attention output's own dequantization, folded straight to int8 because its consumer requantizes it anyway: one rounding per output element, on the same sweep and the same terms as the two rows above. The cost model multiplies it by the attention outputs of every layer and head.

model_constants.dequant_pow2_cells_per_a.note: The part of the power-of-two dequantization that one accumulator costs whatever the row width is. The sweep proves the same 1,048,576 accumulators at 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 per trace row and every point is exactly 15 + 1/width marginal cells, so this is a closed form read off six measurements and not a fit; the row term is the entry below. At the 16-per-row layout the other subcommands use the two give 15.0625, which is the measured power-of-two figure above.

model_constants.dequant_pow2_cells_per_r.note: What a trace row of the power-of-two dequantization costs on top of its accumulators, from the same six-width sweep: one cell, spread over the accumulators the row carries. It is a property of the variant and not of the gadget in general -- on the same sweep's terms the bf16 chain carries two cells a row and the integer reading and the rounding carry none.

model_constants.requant_cells_per_value.note: One requantized value with its scale argument, the marginal cells with the shared tables left out and the two committed input cells left out because the producer commits them. The subcommand proves four points: 8.0625 and 11.4375 for power-of-two scales without and with the argument, 8.125 and 11.5 for bf16. The cost model takes the largest of the two with the argument and charges one less than it per distinct matmul input, because the committed quantized value is already counted.

model_constants.residual_stream_add_cell.note: One correctly rounded bf16 add of the residual stream, the marginal cells with the shared tables and the component's leaves left out. The cost model multiplies it by the two residual adds of every layer and by the adds of each normalisation's reduction. Putting a unary operation in front of the add does not move it: the same 24.3226 with a square on every leaf.

model_constants.residual_stream_mul_cell.note: One bf16 multiply of the residual stream, on the same terms as the add above. The cost model multiplies it by the two multiplies of every normalisation and by the SwiGLU's product. The SiLU in front of the product does not move it, and the normalisation's own scale is 8.4375 because its second operand is a preprocessed weight.

model_constants.argmax_cells_per_compari.note: Proving the emitted token is the argmax costs one comparison per vocabulary entry per token, and this is what one comparison costs: 8 tokens over a vocabulary of 8,192, 64 comparisons a row, of which 3.046875 cells are the committed trace and the rest the lookups. It is the whole gadget over the comparisons; the cost model subtracts an assumed fixed table half of 40,960 cells to reach a per-comparison marginal of 8.421875, and one vocabulary cannot separate the two -- a second one would.

model_constants.attention_cells_per_head.note: What one entry of the attention score grid costs: the committed shift, the exponential's answer and the probability, over 512 tokens and 1,024 keys at head dimension 64. It is exactly 4 at all five instance counts the run packs, 1 through 16, so it is the grid's own price and not an artefact of one packing. It is the whole of the attention term only in the superseded single-slope form; the key tile coefficients are what the cost model charges, and they carry a per-key and a per-token cost this number does not.

model_constants.weight_freivalds_cells_p.note: The weight Freivalds check's committed cells per weight, at the prover's own default row width: `result.points[0].cells.cells_per_weight` of runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b3-freivalds.json. Its three QM31 accumulator columns cost 12 cells a trace row and a row carries p weights, so the law is 12/p and p is a layout knob, not a constant of the gadget: this is 12/136, the default of `params_of`. The sweep beside it, b3-freivalds-widths.json, returns 12/p to the cell at 8, 16, 32 and 64 weights a row, which is what says the closed form holds rather than assuming it. A group of n matmuls shares one accumulator and so costs (4 + 8n)/(n p) per weight and not 12/p, which the cost model does not know: charging 12/p across a layer over-charges the two-matmul group by 20 per cent and the three-matmul one by 29. The private archive's 0.0902 is 12/133, the same law at a shape whose grid padded 32,256 rows up to 2^15, so it is this figure inflated 2.3 per cent by row padding and not a second measurement; this subcommand refuses a ragged tiling and reports the unpadded form.

model_constants.weight_freivalds_preproc.note: The preprocessed side of the same check at the same row width, the trace a proof reads once rather than commits again: `result.points[0].cells.preprocessed_per_weight` of runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b3-freivalds.json. It is exactly 1 + 4/p -- one cell a weight, plus the four selectors amortised over a row -- at 8, 16, 32, 64 and 136 weights a row, so it is the same closed form as the fresh figure beside it. Each point is a marginal over the weights two output widths differ by and carries no row padding; the private archive's 1.0903 is one padded component divided by its weights, from a component that also carried nine preprocessed columns beside its weights where this one carries four. The preprocessed trace is in none of the cost model's cell totals, so this figure moves `moe.<model>.preprocessed_over_fresh` and nothing else.

model_constants.logup_marginal_cells_per.note: The marginal cells one LogUp lookup adds, per lookup batch size: `result.closed_form.marginal_cells_per_lookup` of runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/logup.json and the four points beside it. 4 at batch 1, which every shared table's own side finalizes with, and 2 at batch 2, which every use side does, so it is 4/batch at both sizes this prover uses. Measured on a range check, one committed cell a lookup, and on a pair table lookup, two; the two agree, because an interaction column is one QM31 whatever the relation's arity, so the arity moves what the gadget commits and not the column count. Recorded as an object keyed by the batch size written as a string, because the cost model indexes it by the batch it charges and `cost_model.logup_marginal_by_batch` refuses a scalar.

model_constants.dequant_chain_away_cells.note: Dequantization by the bf16 chain at the rounding away from zero, the marginal cells one accumulator adds with the shared tables left out; 1,048,576 accumulators, 16 per row, from the `chain` point's `cells_per_acc_marginal` in runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b6-dequant-away.json. This is what the cost model charges on all seven layer matmuls, because rounding away from zero is what the quantization configuration specifies and what every recorded proof builds. `model_constants.dequant_chain_cells_per_acc` is the same gadget at the round half to even, 26.125, exactly one cell an accumulator more, and is not this.

model_constants.dequant_pow2_away_cells_.note: Dequantization by a power-of-two scale at the rounding away from zero, on the same sweep and the same terms as the chain entry above, from the `pow2` point's `cells_per_acc_marginal` in runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b6-dequant-away.json. The cost model charges it on the output head. `model_constants.dequant_pow2_cells_per_acc` is the round half to even, 15.0625, again exactly one cell an accumulator more.

model_constants.dequant_chain_away_base_.note: The chain variant's committed columns alone, with the LogUp running sums left to the batched reduction: `columns.base` of the same `chain` point in runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b6-dequant-away.json, 230 columns over the 16 accumulators a trace row carries. That is what a proof with `--gkr-dequant` builds, which is the configuration the paper reports. The round-half-to-even output gives 246/16 = 15.375, one cell an accumulator more, the same difference as on the marginal figures.

model_constants.dequant_pow2_away_base_c.note: The power-of-two variant's committed columns alone, on the same terms as the chain entry above: `columns.base` of the `pow2` point in runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b6-dequant-away.json, 148 columns over 16 accumulators a row. Of the four away figures this is the one the sound statement charges most, because with `--gkr-dequant` on the layer matmuls read the composed price instead and the output head's dequantization is this. The round-half-to-even output gives 164/16 = 10.25.

model_constants.argmax_marginal_cells_pe.note: What one argmax comparison adds, as the slope of fresh cells against comparisons over three vocabularies at the same 8 tokens and the same 64 comparisons a row: 592,896 cells over 65,536 comparisons in runs/2026-09-11-microbench-cells-h100/b10-argmax.json (vocabulary 8,192), 858,112 over 131,072 in b10-argmax-v16k.json and 1,388,544 over 262,144 in b10-argmax-v32k.json, each the strict point's `cells.fresh`. The three are exactly collinear: 4.046875 cells a comparison, and a fixed side of 327,680 cells -- 65,536 of committed trace and 262,144 of interaction -- that does not move with the vocabulary. This is the figure the cost model charges. `model_constants.argmax_cells_per_comparison` is the whole gadget over its comparisons, 9.046875 at the smallest of the three vocabularies, and is not this; subtracting an assumed fixed side of ten interaction columns over the trace rows, which is what the model did until this run, gives 8.421875 and is wrong by the whole of the real fixed side. The private archive's 4.046875 is this same number.

model_constants.int8_range_cells_per_act.note: model_constants.logup_marginal_cells_per_lookup['2'] / 2. The range check on a committed int8 activation is one arity-2 lookup into the 2^16 byte-pair table covering two activations, at the batch size every use side finalizes with; the activations' own committed cells are charged elsewhere. The private archive measured the same 1.0 directly at three sizes, and the byte-at-a-time form it replaced is 2.0.

model_constants.residual_stream_unary_ce.note: 2 + model_constants.logup_marginal_cells_per_lookup['2']. One bf16 unary operation commits its output as one bf16 value, which is two cells, and pays one lookup at pairwise batching. The cost model multiplies it by each normalisation's square and inverse square root and by the SwiGLU's SiLU. The prover reports the same figure under primitives.unary of the residual-stream output, built from the same two terms, so it is an exact count and not a second measurement.

model_constants.dequant_chain_composed_c.note: What the composed prover builds the whole dequantization at, per matmul accumulator: 353,632,256 cells over 22,020,096 accumulators, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. The cells are the committed columns (`family_cells.dequant`) plus what the reduction leaves in the interaction trace (`family_cells.interaction_by_family.dequant.cells`); the accumulators are the segment's own `family_cells.mats[].n` added up. The committed accumulator is in it and the cost model charges that separately as well. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own. `model_constants.dequant_chain_cells_per_acc` is the standalone chain gadget, 26.125 cells with the round half to even, and must not be read for this. Both segments record `params.round: "even"`, so this is the round-half-to-even figure; on the layer matmuls the cost model charges rounding away from zero, which is one cell an accumulator less.

model_constants.requant_composed_cells_p.note: What the composed prover builds the whole requantization at, per distinct matmul input value: 212,664,832 cells over 11,534,336 values, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. The cells are the committed columns of the three seams (`family_cells.requant[].cells.base`), the multiplicity column of their own tables (`family_cells.requant_tables.multiplicity`) and the interaction the reduction leaves (`family_cells.interaction_by_family.requant.cells`); the values are `family_cells.requant[].checked` added up. The committed int8 value and its range check are the producer's and are not in it. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own. `model_constants.requant_cells_per_value` is the standalone gadget, 11.5, and is not this.

model_constants.quant_composed_cells_per.note: What the composed prover builds the quantization of the attention q and k at, per value: 45,875,200 cells over 2,621,440 values, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. The cells are `family_cells.quant[].cells.base` plus `family_cells.interaction_by_family.quant.cells`, the values `family_cells.quant[].checked` added up. No reduction owns this one and no other key names it: until the composed statement was priced the cost model charged nothing for it at all. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own.

model_constants.weight_freivalds_compose.note: What the composed prover builds the Freivalds check of the weight matmuls at, per weight: 44,040,192 cells over 218,103,808 weights, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. The cells are `family_cells.freivalds` plus `family_cells.interaction_by_family.freivalds.cells`, the weights `family_cells.freivalds_weights[].weights` added up. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own. The standalone check is 0.0902 cells a weight at its own design point in the width sweep the cost model still reads from a retired benchmark tree, and the composed check at this statement is more than twice that, most of the difference interaction the reduction does not remove. `model_constants.weight_freivalds_cells_per_weight`, which `microbench-cells` is to measure, is that standalone figure and is not this.

model_constants.attnout_composed_cells_p.note: What the composed prover builds the attention-output fold at, per accumulator: 21,757,952 cells over 2,097,152 accumulators, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. The cells are `family_cells.attnout` plus `family_cells.interaction_by_family.attnout.cells`; the accumulators are the segment's own `params.nh` x `params.hd` x `params.s`, which is the `family_cells.attnout_stats.n` the segment reports. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own. `model_constants.attnout_int8_cells_per_acc` is the standalone fold, 10.0625, and is not this.

model_constants.residual_stream_composed.note: What one bf16 multiply of the residual stream costs in the composed prover: 26,214,400 cells over 5,242,880 multiplies, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. Read off the rope's own two multiplies per rotated value, the `rpqm` and `rpkm` entries of `family_cells.residual_stream_components`, whose `cells` and `ops` the segment reports on their own; they are the only bf16 multiplies a segment counts by themselves. These are the committed columns alone: the 163,840 cells the reduction leaves for the two components are not in it. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own. `model_constants.residual_stream_mul_cells_per_op` is the standalone multiply, 8.75, and is not this.

What one bf16 add of the residual stream costs in the composed prover: 47,185,920 cells over 2,621,440 adds, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. Read off the rope's own add per rotated value, the `rpqa` and `rpka` entries of `family_cells.residual_stream_components`, on the same terms as the multiply above: the committed columns alone, without the 163,840 cells the reduction leaves for the two components. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own. `model_constants.residual_stream_add_cells_per_op` is the standalone add, 24.3226, and is not this.

What one SwiGLU channel costs in the composed prover, one `silu` table application and one bf16 product together: 73,400,320 cells over 7,340,032 channels, on segment B8L16 and on the other 30 non-embedding layer segments of block B8 in runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, and on all 31 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json: the same two integers on all 62, so neither the context nor the card is a variable of it. Layer segment 0 carries the embedding lookup, builds one cell an attention-output accumulator more and is not among them. Read off the `gsw` entry of `family_cells.residual_stream_components`, the committed columns alone, without the 196,608 cells the reduction leaves for it. The table application on its own is this less the multiply beside it, 5. A re-fit against one statement -- Llama-3.1-8B, a block of 512 decoded tokens, spec `b10-final`, all five batched reductions on -- and not a price of the gadget on its own. No standalone key names the unary application: it is a constant of the micro-benchmark and not one of its measurements.

assumption.cost_model.log_table.note: The height of the master exponent table the attention softmax reads, which is 5 x 2^log_table cells and 41,943,040 of the 1,393,069,168 fresh cells of the 8B layer segment the cost model prices, 3.01 per cent of it. The modal value over the 64 layer and first segments of the two headline runs, 32 of them at 23, the rest at 22, 24 and 25, read off segment B8L4 of runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, over that artifact's 32 layer and first segments of token block B8 and the 32 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json; it is a property of the witness the run extracted and not of a card or a context, and the dearest value the two runs carry is 25.

assumption.cost_model.kmax.note: The normalisation table's binades, which is also the fraction table's row count: 5,324,800 cells of that segment, 0.38 per cent of it. The modal value over the 64 layer and first segments of the two headline runs, 64 of them at 19 and none at another value, read off segment B8L0 of runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, over that artifact's 32 layer and first segments of token block B8 and the 32 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json; it is a property of the witness the run extracted and not of a card or a context, and the dearest value the two runs carry is 19.

assumption.cost_model.ao_acc_hi_bits.note: The high half of the attention output accumulator's measured exponent range, one of the three range tables the fold builds; the three together are 5,243,120 cells of that segment, 0.38 per cent of it. The modal value over the 64 layer and first segments of the two headline runs, 23 of them at 5, the rest at 4, 6, 7 and 8, read off segment B8L4 of runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, over that artifact's 32 layer and first segments of token block B8 and the 32 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json; it is a property of the witness the run extracted and not of a card or a context, and the dearest value the two runs carry is 6.

assumption.cost_model.ao_acc_lo_bits.note: The low half of the same accumulator's measured exponent range, which carries its own range table: 327,680 cells of that segment, 0.02 per cent of it. The modal value over the 64 layer and first segments of the two headline runs, 64 of them at 16 and none at another value, read off segment B8L0 of runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, over that artifact's 32 layer and first segments of token block B8 and the 32 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json; it is a property of the witness the run extracted and not of a card or a context, and the dearest value the two runs carry is 16.

assumption.cost_model.ao_rem_bits.note: The width of the attention output's remainder range table, one of the three the fold builds; the output head is a different plan and its own four recorded segments agree on 15, which is what the count charges a head segment. The modal value over the 64 layer and first segments of the two headline runs, 64 of them at 20 and none at another value, read off segment B8L0 of runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, over that artifact's 32 layer and first segments of token block B8 and the 32 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json; it is a property of the witness the run extracted and not of a card or a context, and the dearest value the two runs carry is 20.

assumption.cost_model.ao_q_bits.note: The width of the attention output's quotient range table: 30,720 cells of that segment, 0.002 per cent of it. The modal value over the 64 layer and first segments of the two headline runs, 64 of them at 11 and none at another value, read off segment B8L0 of runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, over that artifact's 32 layer and first segments of token block B8 and the 32 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json; it is a property of the witness the run extracted and not of a card or a context, and the dearest value the two runs carry is 11.

assumption.cost_model.ao_jo_min.note: The low end of the attention output's measured exponent window jo, which with ao_jo_max sizes one of the three range tables the fold builds. The modal value over the 64 layer and first segments of the two headline runs, 32 of them at -12, the rest at -14, -13, -11 and -10, read off segment B8L5 of runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, over that artifact's 32 layer and first segments of token block B8 and the 32 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json; it is a property of the witness the run extracted and not of a card or a context, and the dearest value the two runs carry is -14.

assumption.cost_model.ao_jo_max.note: The high end of the attention output's measured exponent window jo, the other end of the window ao_jo_min opens. The modal value over the 64 layer and first segments of the two headline runs, 34 of them at -10, the rest at -12, -11, -9 and -8, read off segment B8L4 of runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, over that artifact's 32 layer and first segments of token block B8 and the 32 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json; it is a property of the witness the run extracted and not of a card or a context, and the dearest value the two runs carry is -12.

assumption.cost_model.ao_jv_min.note: The low end of the attention value's measured exponent window jv; the exponent window the fold's range tables cover is ao_jv minus ao_jo. The modal value over the 64 layer and first segments of the two headline runs, 40 of them at -7, the rest at -11, -10, -9, -8 and -6, read off segment B8L7 of runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, over that artifact's 32 layer and first segments of token block B8 and the 32 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json; it is a property of the witness the run extracted and not of a card or a context, and the dearest value the two runs carry is -11.

assumption.cost_model.ao_jv_max.note: The high end of the attention value's measured exponent window jv, the other end of the window ao_jv_min opens. The modal value over the 64 layer and first segments of the two headline runs, 44 of them at -5, the rest at -8, -6 and -4, read off segment B8L1 of runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, over that artifact's 32 layer and first segments of token block B8 and the 32 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json; it is a property of the witness the run extracted and not of a card or a context, and the dearest value the two runs carry is -8.

assumption.cost_model.fold_rem_bits.note: The width of the fold's own remainder range table: 163,840 cells of that segment, 0.01 per cent of it. The modal value over the 64 layer and first segments of the two headline runs, 64 of them at 15 and none at another value, read off segment B8L0 of runs/2026-09-09-headline-c4096-h100/slice_0256.json, over that artifact's 32 layer and first segments of token block B8 and the 32 of block B32 in runs/2026-09-08-headline-c16384-h100/slice_1024.json; it is a property of the witness the run extracted and not of a card or a context, and the dearest value the two runs carry is 15.

assumption.cost_model.head_groups.note: The prover's --head-groups, which decides the three key grids' heights: both headline runs proved 32 attention heads as 16, 8, 8, so a shape's heads are assumed to be a half and two quarters. Asserted and not measured because it is a knob of a run that has not been made and no witness fixes it; grouping all the heads into one grid instead costs 0.08 per cent less on the 8B layer segment.

assumption.cost_model.kv_per_head.note: Where a key and a value are committed, which is the key cache, the value cache and the boundary trees that hand them on: `LayoutChan` and `LayoutKey` are built from `Shape::chans()` and `Shape::keys()`, both at the attention head count, and `boundary.rs`'s `kv_sides` hands on a cache of that width, so the count charges them once per attention head and not once per key/value head, and it is asserted because no AIR here shares a key tile's K and V columns between two heads' score grids -- on the 8B layer segment that term is 109,051,904 cells and 7.83 per cent of it, and a prover that shared it across the four heads of a group would commit 81,788,928 cells fewer, 5.87 per cent of the segment.

assumption.cost_model.variant.note: The attention softmax the count prices, which costs an auxiliary column a score and a range table: every composed segment of the two headline runs carries intexp. Asserted and not measured because it is the statement a run of another shape would be proved at and no run of one exists; a shape proved at another variant is a different statement.

assumption.cost_model.round.note: The rounding the count prices, which decides the sticky bit of every rounding: every composed segment of the two headline runs carries round half to even. Asserted and not measured for the same reason as assumption.cost_model.variant, that it is the statement a run of another shape would be proved at and no run of one exists.

assumption.cost_model.moe_routing.note: How a mixture layer's tokens are spread over its experts, which decides how many tokens each routed matmul covers and so its rows. Asserted because no run of any of these mixture models has been proved; the model's own words for it, measured on Qwen3-235B-A22B, one mixture layer segment at C=4,096, S=512, worth 322,437,120 cells and 13.63 per cent of the segment: "every token's top-k is taken uniform over the 128 experts, so a segment of 512 tokens touches 128.0 of them and each routed matmul covers 32 tokens. `cells` is what the assumption is worth: the same token slots concentrated on 8 experts of 512 tokens each cost 2,042,494,064 against 2,364,931,184.  Routing statistics from an actual run of the model remove the assumption: pass them as --routing FILE and the row is counted at them".

assumption.cost_model.moe_router.note: How the router itself is charged: its gate matmul is counted from the layout like any other matmul, and the top-k selection on the logits is stated beside the row as a bound rather than charged in it. Asserted, and an upper bound and not a point estimate, because no AIR in this project builds a selection argument; the model's own words for it, on the same Qwen3-235B-A22B segment, worth 5,341,184 cells and 0.23 per cent of the segment: "the gate logits are a matmul of 128 outputs over every token and are COUNTED like any other (3,219,456 cells a segment). The top-k selection on them is not: no AIR here builds one, so it is an upper bound, 8 argmax passes over 128 logits a token at the built gadget's measured marginal (4.046875 cells a comparison, `model_constants.argmax_marginal_cells_per_comparison`), 2,121,728 cells a segment".

assumption.cost_model.mla_form.note: Where a latent attention applies the low-rank pair `kv_b`, which decides what a key costs the cache and how wide the score grid is: the count records the materialised layout, which expands the keys and the values per head before the attention at 40,960 cells a key and 192 channels a head, and it is asserted because no AIR in this project proves either layout -- the same DeepSeek-V3 layer segment at C=4,096, S=512 counted absorbed is 4,988,734,576 cells against 4,104,984,688, so the choice is worth 883,749,888 cells and 21.53 per cent of it.

assumption.cost_model.mla_cache_per_tile.note: How many copies of a shared cache one segment commits under the absorbed layout: a key tile is a component and commits the columns it reads, so the three head groups each hold the latent of every key in their own tile, and it is asserted because no AIR here builds a cache component shared between grids -- on the recorded row it costs no cells at all, because the materialised layout holds a K and a V per head and shares nothing, and one shared channel component and grid would commit 131,334,144 cells fewer than the three.

assumption.cost_model.mla_latent_norm.value: the output head's plain norm at the rank's width
assumption.cost_model.mla_latent_norm.note: What program the two low-rank norms build, `q_a_layernorm` and `kv_a_layernorm` being config fields where the program is not: the count builds the one the output head's final norm already builds, a squares tree with its second-level reduction and a scale, at 1,536 and 512 channels instead of the model's width, and it is asserted because no recorded segment shows a norm at a low rank -- it is 30,205,952 cells and 0.74 per cent of the DeepSeek-V3 layer segment at C=4,096, S=512.

assumption.cost_model.mla_seams.value: one requantize seam per rank the chain passes
assumption.cost_model.mla_seams.note: Where the low-rank chain is requantized: the second matmul of a pair reads what the first wrote, so the rank is requantized between them exactly as the residual is before the projections, at `qkv` 7,168, `q_lat` 1,536 and `kv_lat` 512 on a DeepSeek-V3 layer, and it is asserted because no recorded segment carries a seam at a rank and a layout that carried the rank dequantized would not build them -- it is 27,852,800 cells and 0.68 per cent of that same segment.

cells.b9_prefill.c256.key_tiles.note: Committed cells of the attention key tiles in one segment at a block length of 256 with the context equal to it, on a synthetic layer of 2 key tiles covering 4 attention heads of 32 channels, under the softmax variant `intsplit6`. The diagonal block is on, which at C = S is one more tile per prefix tile, so this is twice the attention score block on its own. The variant is not the one the paper reports: a synthetic layer under the paper's `intexp` cannot be proved at any of these block lengths, because its exponential table is sized from its own data and clamped to 2^22 rows while the data needs 23 (zk-prover #72). The two variants could not be compared, so this number is the key-tile cost of the shape and variant named and not of the paper's.

design.prefill_key_tile_s_squared.note: The coefficient of the squared block length in the key tiles' cost, fitted over the 4 points above with the context equal to the block length. The fit is exact: the largest residual over four points spanning eight times in the block length is 0 cells, so this is a closed form read off a measurement and not a regression. The variant is not the one the paper reports: a synthetic layer under the paper's `intexp` cannot be proved at any of these block lengths, because its exponential table is sized from its own data and clamped to 2^22 rows while the data needs 23 (zk-prover #72). design.prefill_key_tile_s.note: The coefficient of the block length itself, from the same exact fit. At the context equal to the block length the cost model's separate terms in the context and in the block length multiply the same quantity, so what is separable here is these two coefficients and not the three the model carries. The variant is not the one the paper reports: a synthetic layer under the paper's `intexp` cannot be proved at any of these block lengths, because its exponential table is sized from its own data and clamped to 2^22 rows while the data needs 23 (zk-prover #72). cells.b9_prefill_8b.s64c64.key_tiles.note: Committed cells of the attention key tiles in one segment at a block length of 64 with a prefix of 64 keys, on a synthetic layer at the 8B model's own attention width -- 32 attention heads of 128 channels in three key tile groups, every matmul 4,096 by 4,096 -- under the softmax variant `intexp`, which is the arithmetic the paper reports. The sound defaults tile the prefix in blocks of the block length and add one square diagonal block, so this counts 2 key tiles per head group. The exponential table is 2^24 rows, the width the flag asked for, and the attention output's remainder is 22 bits. This is the field `family_cells.key_tiles`, the same one the cost model's own key tile check compares against. The proofs are made on the host's cores under the reference backend and the card is idle throughout; the machine reports an H200, which is what the run id names, and no timing figure from this run is recorded. A cell count does not depend on the card.

cells.b9_prefill_8b.s64c64.key_tiles_fre.note: The same key tiles counting their interaction columns too: the committed cells above plus this segment's interaction rollup entry for them, 254,976 cells. It is 1.0 per cent of the whole segment's committed cells. The proofs are made on the host's cores under the reference backend and the card is idle throughout; the machine reports an H200, which is what the run id names, and no timing figure from this run is recorded. attention_grid.base_cell_coeffs.unit: cells per S*C, per C, per S
attention_grid.base_cell_coeffs.note: The prefix key tile's committed cells at the 8B model's attention width, as the (S*C, C, S) triple the cost model reads: cells = 64 S C + 12288 C + 128 S. Solved from the three points above, whose key tiles cost 64 (S C + S^2) + 12288 C + 12416 S in total; the triple is that total under the composition the cost model itself uses, a prefix key tile at (S, C) plus the same tile at (S, S) with the per-token component dropped. Every coefficient is an identity of the layout at 32 heads of 128: 64 is two per head, 12288 is three per head and channel, 128 is four per head. With the context equal to the block length the C and S columns are the same quantity, so the point at a block of 256 with a prefix of 4,096 is what separates them; three points and three coefficients is an exact solve, so the residual is zero by construction and is not a check of the form. The proofs are made on the host's cores under the reference backend and the card is idle throughout; the machine reports an H200, which is what the run id names, and no timing figure from this run is recorded. A cell count does not depend on the card.

secs.headline.c4096.extract.note: The five layer passes over the whole sequence, added up: the job extracts the whole witness set once and then proves it. The head dumps are one further pass and the driver does not time it, so it is not in this number.

secs.headline.c16384.extract_prove.note: The prove sweep's extraction, added up over the seven groups of token blocks: the extraction whose dumps the 1,058 proofs read. The witness set does not fit the host at this context, so the job extracts a group, proves it and deletes it; a group extracted twice counts once, at its last extraction, which is why this is 9,735 s and not the 9,683 s of the first pass's seven rows in groups.jsonl. The head dumps are one further pass and the driver does not time it.

secs.headline.c16384.extract_survey.note: The survey sweep's extraction, added up over the same seven groups. This run extracted twice: an emitter reads a segment's dump to lower its shape, so the kernels have to be emitted while the dumps are there, and the survey sweep is the pass that writes the shape tables and emits the kernels. It is what the grouping arrangement costs and no proof reads its dumps, so the cold rows do not count it.

secs.headline.c4096.cold_whole_wall.note: secs.headline.c4096.extract + secs.headline.c4096.whole_wall. What the sequence costs on a host that holds no witness dump yet: the extraction the proofs read and the proving scope, one after the other. Emitting the device kernels, installing them and rebuilding are not in it, and no artifact of this run times them.

secs_per_position.headline.c4096.cold_wh.note: secs.headline.c4096.cold_whole_wall / positions.headline.c4096. The same position with the extraction counted in at the whole-wall scope: 14 per cent above secs_per_position.headline.c4096.whole_wall.

usd_per_1k_positions.headline.c4096.cold.note: secs.headline.c4096.cold_whole_wall / positions.headline.c4096, at cost.h100_reference_usd_per_hour. The rate is a published list price and names its source; the card was rented at another price and that price is not a number about this measurement.

secs.headline.c4096.cold_loop.note: secs.headline.c4096.extract + secs.headline.c4096.loop. Emitting the device kernels, installing them and rebuilding are not in it, and no artifact of this run times them.

secs_per_position.headline.c4096.cold_lo.note: secs.headline.c4096.cold_loop / positions.headline.c4096. What one proved position cost on a host that holds no witness dump yet: the extraction the proofs read and the segment loop, one after the other. It is 21 per cent above secs_per_position.headline.c4096.loop, which prices the proving alone.
